sections.text: Quantum LEAP Conference 2025

In 2025, LEAP took place in Phoenix, Arizona. Surrounded by the desert landscape and guided by the theme "Unleash Human Potential," we set out to create a visual identity that captured both the heat and energy of the region. As AI continues to grow in influence, we wanted to emphasize something deeper, that our focus remains on people, and on celebrating human success.

text: Art Direction, Motion, Video: Steve Fisher
Illustration, Design: Steve Fisher, Michael Moulton, Maciej Krupa

sections.text: Conference branding

I built the 2025 brand system around elements that reflected the Phoenix setting. This year's identity was more vibrant, with dynamic, energetic shapes and a richer color palette. The inspiration came directly from the intense Arizona sun and the movement of desert heat, translated into design that felt bold, fresh, and alive.
LEAP 25 brand
Key elements
Art Direction - Steve Fisher | Illustration - Maciej Krupa
Promotion
Motion - Steve Fisher | Graphic - Maciej Krupa
Web

The landing page for LEAP 2025 was more intentional from the start. I designed the web experience to serve as the first introduction to the brand — a strong, immersive entry point. Big, expressive colors set the tone, echoing the energy and warmth attendees would experience at the live event.
Experience

The LEAP 2025 experience was electric. Every touchpoint felt considered and consistent with the larger brand story. Once again, I led on-site video production and managed our event photographer. I also brought our keynote presentations to life, using motion design to elevate static mockups and make our product feel more tangible and real on stage.
LEAP Intro deliverable - motion - Steve Fisher | Script – Mads Herring

sections.text: Quantum LEAP Conference 2024

In 2024, LEAP took place in New Orleans, LA. With the theme "Simplicity Reimagined, Efficiency Redefined," we set out to blend the spirit of jazz with the precision of tech. Our goal was to transform an otherwise standard hotel conference room into an immersive and memorable experience. From the first impression to the final moment, the LEAP brand was present in every detail, creating a cohesive journey that felt both intentional and inspired.

text: Art Direction, Motion, Video: Steve Fisher
Illustration: Steve Fisher, Michael Moulton, Maciej Krupa

sections.text: LEAP Intro deliverable - motion - Steve Fisher | Script – Mads Herring
Conference branding

Building off the strong brand system we developed in 2023, we were able to move more efficiently and intentionally into the 2024 identity. Our goal was to create a visual experience that felt distinct from the previous year. We introduced a cinematic color palette using cyan and Quantum Metric magenta, setting a bold and modern tone. Repeating shapes and a frosted glass effect became key elements in our system, helping us build layered compositions that felt fresh and dimensional. Even though the designs were created in 2D, the layering approach added depth that translated seamlessly across both digital and physical spaces.
2024 Direction
Simplicity reimagined. Efficiency redefined.
Creative Direction - Michael Moulton | Art Direction, Motion Design - Steve Fisher
Video

Like the previous year, I led the design and production of on-stage graphics and videos, bringing our product visualizations to life in a dynamic, engaging way. I was also on-site to produce video content throughout the event, handling same-day edits to quickly capture and share the energy and key moments from each day. In addition to content creation, I oversaw our hired event photographer, ensuring the visual coverage aligned with our brand and marketing goals.
Experience

Every moment of the event included a thoughtful brand touchpoint crafted by the Studio team. From the digital stage screens to product demos and even the award designs, each element was built to reflect the identity and energy of the event. The vibrant spirit of New Orleans came through in all of it, adding depth and authenticity to the experience.
LEAP 2024 Recap

sections.text: Quantum LEAP Conference 2023

In 2023, Quantum Metric brought its flagship conference, LEAP, fully in-house for the first time. This shift marked a pivotal moment for the brand, prompting a refreshed visual identity and greater creative ownership. I led the art direction for both the new LEAP logo and the design system for the 2023 conference.

text: Art Direction, Motion, Video: Steve Fisher

sections.text: LEAP Intro deliverable - motion - Steve Fisher | Script – Mads Herring
Conference branding

Since this was our first in-person conference after the pandemic, we wanted the experience to be beautiful, especially in such a well-known space. We had a clear direction from the start, and the brand was built around the theme: "Guided Empathy, Endless Impact." How is empathy visualized? Being in a venue with such a deep musical history helped shape that answer. Sound waves felt like the perfect symbol. They bounce off one another, overlap, and build into something more. That idea became the foundation for the visual identity of the event.
2023 Direction
Guided empathy, endless impact.
Compassionate empathy goes beyond simply understanding others and sharing their feelings: it actually moves us to take action, to help however we can.
Event Photography, Motion – Steve Fisher | Graphic, Jason McAloon
Brand strategy

From the beginning, the goal for LEAP was to feel bigger than we were. One of the best ways to do that was by expanding the brand palette to create a more unique and immersive experience. We introduced purple and navy tones and used gradients that faded smoothly into each other, giving the visuals a polished and dynamic feel. For the LEAP logo, we moved away from the blocky, paper-inspired imagery used in earlier versions. We wanted a mark that could stand on its own but still feel like part of the Quantum Metric brand. It needed to be flexible enough to work in any location or context, while still being instantly recognizable.
Experience

We had to lead our marketing efforts with a clear goal– convince people and companies that it was worth investing in sending their teams back to in-person events. Our last two conferences were virtual, so this was a big shift. To help bridge that gap, we pulled in footage from past events and combined it with more stylized, energetic slides. The goal was to build excitement and momentum. We wanted to show the best version of our brand for this first post-pandemic conference.
Photography

I was on-site at LEAP to capture photography and video content that would power the marketing for the following year's event. My focus was on documenting the energy, emotion, and scale of the experience. Everything from the keynote moments to candid interactions between attendees. At the same time, I kept a clear eye on what kinds of visuals would be most valuable for future promotional use. That meant thinking ahead: capturing content with next year's campaigns, ads, and brand storytelling in mind, not just what looked good in the moment.

sections.text: Quantum Metric - Felix AI

Our product team was figuring out how to incorporate first-to-market AI into our platform. Directed from our CEO, we worked on turning Felix into reality through our brand identity, product, and in many of our touch points.

text: Art Direction, Motion, Video: Steve Fisher, Nick Ritter
Illustration, Design: Steve Fisher, Michael Moulton, Maciej Krupa

sections.text: Felix AI - Branding & Mascot

Just like every SaaS offering, our product team was figuring out how to incorporate AI into our platform. Our CEO, who was inspired by a fox that visited his backyard frequently, was set on Felix.
We were given the task of turning Felix not only into a part of our brand, but also into a mascot that can be used as the face of our AI-powered features. I was in charge of designing the look of Felix. I sketched and concepted the first versions. We handed Felix off to a modeler for the final passes.
Art Direction - Steve Fisher
Web

Our first implementation for Felix was our webinar series. This series was our introduction into how we were going to release our AI offering. Because our product was first-to-industry, we set out to make our landing page to make a big splash. We implemented Spline for the Felix head on the landing page. He added a bit of wow-factor to our series. It was one of our top performing webinars to date.
Art Direction, Web Design - Steve Fisher | Development - Brad Douglas

sections.text: Peak Benchmark Report

Last year, our PR manager Lori Niquette began gathering industry data to support our thought leadership efforts. To help that content stand out, we elevated the visuals through an interactive landing page that brought the insights to life in a more engaging, memorable way.

text: Art Direction, Motion, Design: Steve Fisher

sections.text: Technology

One of our key goals in 2024 was to bring new technology into our web experience. We incorporated Spline for interactive 3D elements and used SVG animations powered by GreenSock to create smooth, dynamic line animations. The result was a visually striking, data-driven story that not only elevated our design but also deeply resonated with our customers.

sections.text: Quantum Metric | Web Refresh
I refreshed Quantum Metric's site with a scalable, component-driven system. We incorporated Tailwind CSS for clean, reusable styling. We saw an increase overall in qualified leads as a result.
Visit quantummetric.com

sections.text: Scalable design-thinking.

I took a design system that was clunky and hard to maintain and rebuilt it into something scalable. By standardizing components, creating clear tokens, and tightening up the rules around layout and styling, the system became flexible enough to support hundreds of pages without breaking consistency. What used to be a mess of one-off fixes is now a foundation that actually grows with the product.
Screens
Benchmark Reports

We've had the opportunity to create more experiential benchmark reports each quarter. This has allowed us to try new things and implement different types of technologies like GSAP, Spline, and AGcharts.

sections.text: Adobe Workfront | Web Refresh

We were handed an agency special. At least 30 different hex codes for the same orange. Before we even started, our team did an audit of low-performing pages. We found countless pages we were serving up to be underperforming. From here we took on the challenge of building out our CMS with reusable components, a language that was clear to both design and development, and templates that were high-performing and looked good.
After Workfront was acquired the content was ported to Adobe's website.
Visit the old Workfront website on the webarchive.
